model_annotation: The figure presents a donut-style pie chart illustrating the distribution of 1,100 tasks across nine distinct capabilities, as described in the paper "Can Language Models Follow Multiple Turns of Entangled Instructions." The chart is organized into three concentric rings: the outermost ring contains six capabilities—Prioritization (100), Personalization (100), Privacy Protection (111), Multitasking (160), Dynamic Instruction (100), and Memorization (100)—each labeled with a numerical value indicating the number of tasks assigned to that capability. The middle ring includes three additional capabilities: Dynamic Environment (100), Recursive Reasoning (110), and Triggering (100). The innermost ring, forming the core of the chart, displays two central capabilities: Context Tracking (in dark blue) and Contradiction Resolution (in dark red), with Context Retrieving (in dark green) positioned between them. The segments are color-coded and connected to their respective labels via lines, with the values clearly displayed next to each label. The chart visually emphasizes that while most capabilities have approximately 100 tasks, Multitasking has the highest count (160), followed by Privacy Protection (111) and Recursive Reasoning (110), indicating slight imbalances despite the overall aim for balanced sample distribution. The design suggests a hierarchical or layered structure of capabilities, with the innermost ring possibly representing foundational or core functions.
